text:
lia: Quick snapshot — microbench for helix9b-lite (chat workload) int8 vs int6. Product asked for ~20% unit-cost cut but <1.5% quality delta. Putting numbers here for a quick GTN recommendation.

siva: paste the numbers when you have them — curious about long context behavior too.

lia: TL;DR: int6 gives ~37% cost reduction vs int8 but shows small quality regressions on our product eval sets. Details: 
- p50 latency (single-turn, 512 tokens): int8=140ms, int6=118ms.
- p95 latency: int8=370ms, int6=320ms.
- cost / 1M tokens (raw infra): int8=$34.8, int6=$21.9.
- QA pass (scored GTN rubric top-1): int8=92.1%, int6=90.0% (delta -2.1%).
- Longform recall (512-2048 tokens): int8=88.4, int6=87.6 (delta -0.8).
- Prefix/KV caching helps both, but int6 shows slightly higher next-token entropy on long prefixes.

jamal: Useful. So unit econ: ~$12.9 saved per 1M tokens (~37%). But quality delta is ~2.1% on our primary GTN rubric — above product target. Do we have slice-level breakdowns? any specific intents hit worse?

lia: Slice breakdown quick notes: 
- Short QA (<=64 tokens): int6 ~ parity (-0.2%).
- Multi-step instructions (200-600 tokens): int6 -3.3% (worst).
- Code/formatting style tasks: int6 -1.5%.
- Safety/regulatory prompts: parity (within noise).

emily: From product perspective, multi-step instruction degradation is the main blocker. Users notice when follow-ups lose specificity. But $12.9 / 1M tokens is material for pricing. Possible play: hybrid routing or dynamic gating based on intent/length.

jamal: Proposal: default int6 for low-risk slices (short QA, safety checks, embeddings-adjacent flows) and pin int8 for multi-step and longform. Rough split estimate: 65% int6 / 35% int8 => blended cost saving ~24% and quality drop ~0.8% on global metric (estimate).

siva: I like the hybrid. A couple ops notes: 1) need canary for int6 with traffic splits and per-route SLOs; 2) watch latency tail — int6 p95 improved but p99 needs more samples.

lia: Canary checklist: 
- Start 5% traffic, slice guard for multi-step intents -> route to int8.
- Monitor GTN rubric buckets and new user-facing regressions (A/B eval harness).
- Cost telemetry: token-level spend by route, unit econ calc daily.
- Auto-fallback: if daily QA delta >1.5% or p95 latency regresses >10% -> rollback.

emily: Also want a short scorecard to present to GTN/product: include baseline numbers, blended econ projection (65/35 and 80/20), expected UX delta, and recommended rollout plan. Can someone draft?

lia: I can draft the scorecard today. Quick sketch: 
- Baseline (int8): cost= $34.8 / 1M, GTN=92.1%
- Int6 baseline: cost= $21.9 / 1M, GTN=90.0%
- 65/35 hybrid: cost≈$27.6 / 1M (~20.7% saving), projected GTN≈91.3% (est).
- 80/20 hybrid: cost≈$25.6 / 1M (~26.5% saving), projected GTN≈90.7%
- Recommendation: start 65/35 canary for 2 weeks + gated intents.

ops-bot: Deploy canary job queued: canary/helix9b-lite-int6-hybrid -> starts at 2026-03-25T14:00Z (ETA). Monitor channel: #eng-runtime-canaries.

jamal: One more ask: include a small evaluation on prompt prefixing to see if priming reduces the multi-step penalty for int6 (hypothesis: targeted priming recovers ~0.6-1.0% GTN). If so, we can keep higher int6 fraction.

lia: noted — will run a targeted priming sweep (1000 samples) and update the scorecard by EOD tomorrow.

emily: Thanks team — if priming helps, product is OK with 75%+ int6. If not, start 65/35 and re-evaluate after 2 weeks.

lia: I'll post the draft scorecard link here when ready. Thanks for the quick input :thumbsup:
